parts.note: a yarn is a spun thread
unadorned means plain or bare

explanation.surface: A tired old story told without embellishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' reads as a story in the surface but here is the spun fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothes are worn out, so figuratively a threadbare joke or argument is stale and overused.

clue.text: Child has a point to convey

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A youngster who has a message to get across.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote something is to carry it, which is to convey it.

clue.text: City of almost three million, possibly more

indicators.note: possibly says the word more may be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A city of nearly three million people, maybe more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly more' reads as a population estimate, but 'possibly' rearranges MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's capital has a population of a little under three million.

parts.note: ado is fuss or bustle
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something revered for its lively activity and vivid hue.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love or revere them as if a god.

parts.note: the proverb says similar creatures flock together, and sheep flock, so they behave like sheep

explanation.surface: A saying about people who behave in a shy, embarrassed way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepishly' suggests embarrassment, but it means acting like sheep, which flock together.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says like-minded people group together, just as sheep keep to a flock.

clue.text: Turned and fled with detectives in pursuit

indicators.note: in pursuit means the detectives come after the word for fled

parts.note: fled means ran away
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A fugitive turned and ran with the police chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like an action in the chase, but it means gone sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned has gone off, which is to say it smells rotten.

clue.text: He has writing dictated by the height of fashion

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A man whose words are written down at the command of the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Height of fashion' reads as the latest style, but it is the hemline, whose height fashion sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt's hemline is where its length sits, which fashion raises and lowers each season.

clue.text: Sends a plea for restoration of seaside walks

indicators.note: restoration of the letters means putting them back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone appeals for the repair of old seafront promenades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For restoration of' rearranges SENDS A PLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long level promenade, typically along a seafront.

parts.note: read as used, meaning not new, and as the pointer on a watch that counts off seconds

explanation.surface: Something worn on duty by a sentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' is both pre-owned and in use, and 'watch' is a timepiece rather than guard duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods carry this label, and the thin pointer counting seconds on a watch bears the same name.

clue.text: Rambo tune I transpose for single instrument

indicators.note: to transpose is to shift around, so these letters change position

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a Rambo theme tune for a solo instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transpose' is musical in the surface but rearranges RAMBO TUNE I.
explanation.definitionFit: The tambourine is a hand-held percussion instrument, a frame drum with jingles.

clue.text: The story's only part of the whole picture

indicators.note: only part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A narrative gives just a fragment of the full view.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic narrative poem or saga is called by this name.

explanation.surface: Key facts about celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable points in a report; read whimsically, lights high in the sky, such as stars.

clue.text: Firm assurance about end of term settlement

indicators.note: about means going round, so the firm and the assurance surround the letter

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a promise is an assurance

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of term

explanation.surface: A company's guarantee concerning the close of a contract period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective but is the company. 'About' wraps the firm and the assurance round M, the end of 'term'.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is an agreement reached by both sides giving ground, a settlement of a dispute.

clue.text: Blackfoot, for example, strange though it may seem

definitions.text: Blackfoot, for example, strange though it may seem

parts.words: Blackfoot, for example, strange though it may seem
parts.note: the Blackfoot are a Native American people, once called by an old colour-based term, which is odd given their black name

explanation.surface: A remark on how oddly a people are named.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the clash of colours: a people called Blackfoot fall under an old term meaning red. The term is now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: This dated, now offensive term referred to Native Americans, of whom the Blackfoot are one people.

parts.note: in card games, failing to play a card of the led suit when able breaks the rules

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to copy what everyone else does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow suit' is the idiom for copying others; here it is literal card play.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist, a player who revokes fails to follow the led suit despite holding a card of it.

indicators.note: needing treatment suggests the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wounds on someone's torso require medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Need treatment' rearranges ON CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Notches are small V-shaped cuts in an edge or surface.

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other
distress here means to damage or knock out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone pushed on through terrible hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' scrambles the word for dreadful into IRED, and 'amid' sets the little word 'on' in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed clothes have been smoothed with a hot iron.

annotationWithheld.why: 'Murder mother for the estate': the parse is MA inside DO IN, but no clue word signals the insertion ('for' only links the definition), so the container has no indicator

parts.note: literally, the pledge that physicians take on qualifying; idiomatically, something they trust

explanation.surface: Medics strongly recommend a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear by' means trust in, but here it is literal: the pledge doctors recite.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ethical pledge named after an ancient Greek physician, traditionally taken by new medics.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other letters go round the honour

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A young woman is abandoned without recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside: 'is' plus the abbreviation for left wrap round the British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, a Scottish form of Elizabeth.

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin librae
to make money is to earn

explanation.surface: Someone finds that money breeds more money.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'money' is L, the pound sign's letter; 'makes money' is EARNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn a fact is to find it out, to discover it.

indicators.note: roughly suggests the word veers is rendered loosely, in a new order

explanation.surface: A river swerves, more or less heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges the word for swerves into SEVER. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a river flowing from Wales through western England.

parts.note: address as a speech rather than where the vicar lives

explanation.surface: Where the parish priest lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' wants to be a location, the vicarage; it is a speech from the pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a talk on religion delivered by a cleric during a service.

indicators.note: to assemble is to put together, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: Regional assemblies gather in the German city of Essen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assemble' reads as a verb for the councils meeting, but it rearranges AT ESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a governing council or legislative chamber, as in several US states.

clue.text: He takes after his father, presumably

definitions.text: He takes after his father, presumably

parts.words: He takes after his father, presumably
parts.note: takes after as succeeds rather than resembles; presumably hints at the presumptive successor

explanation.surface: A son who probably resembles his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes after' means resembles in the surface, but here it means comes after, inheriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A son who inherits on his father's death succeeds him; 'presumably' nods to an heir presumptive.

clue.text: A mother for one who was motherless

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal

explanation.surface: A mother adopts a child who had none.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the first man was made from dust, so had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the first man was created directly by God, with no parents.

clue.text: A drug addict, perhaps, makes sure

indicators.note: makes means the word sure is fashioned into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An addict checks something is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' turns SURE into its anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug taker is often called this; the 'perhaps' shows an addict is one example.

clue.text: Man of principle made riches in a way

indicators.note: in a way means in some fashion, so the letters are set out differently

explanation.surface: A principled man who somehow got rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of principle' sounds like an honest man but means the Greek who gave his name to a principle of buoyancy. 'In a way' rearranges MADE RICHES.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek scientist is famed for the buoyancy principle named after him.

explanation.surface: Something leaps from the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive from or arise; and the forward-most timber of a ship, its prow.

parts.note: read as someone who watches the night sky rather than a security guard

explanation.surface: A guard on the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A night-watchman guards a building, but here it is one who studies the night sky. In cricket the term also names a late-order batsman sent in near close of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies stars and planets, chiefly observing after dark.
